newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Mitsubishi to build Saudi methanol plant.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi to build Saudi methanol plant.

text.p: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries of Japan on Monday signed a contract to build a fourth methanol plant for the Saudi Methanol Company (Ar-Razi), Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said.

"Ar-Razi, an affiliate of SABIC, today (Monday) signed a contract with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries of Japan for the construction of a new world-scale chemical grade methanol plant at its complex in al-Jubail industrial city," SABIC said in a statement.
Ar-Razi signed a letter of intent with Mitsubishi in March to build the 850,000 metric tonnes plant which would come on stream in May 1999.
"Today's agreement marks the final award of the lump sum contract for the 850,000 metric tonnes a year plant," the statement said.

Ar-Razi, which operates the world's biggest methanol complex with a current annual capacity of 1.4 million tonnes, is a 50-50 joint venture between SABIC and a consortium of Japanese firms led by Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company.
SABIC's vice-president and managing director Ibrahim bin Salameh said world demand for methanol was expected to continue to grow.

"Although global demand for methanol is not increasing at the same pace as a couple of years ago, it is still growing, and SABIC is well placed to produce and supply more methanol to the world market," Bin Salameh said in the statement.
He said Ar-Razi's third 850,000-tonnes-a-year plant was due to begin trial production next month and would raise the company's capacity to 2.25 million tonnes of methanol.
When the fourth plant is completed, it would raise Ar-Razi's production capacity to 3.1 million tonnes annually.

Industrial giant SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, controls and operates 16 complexes with Western and Japanese companies producing more than 23 million tonnes a year of petrochemical, plastic, fertiliser and steel.
